## Why This Is Asked

This question evaluates your ability to combine two simple data structures into a practical, efficient solution. It tests understanding of amortized analysis, edge-case handling, and how to track auxiliary information (min values) alongside primary data.

## Key Concepts

- **Deque semantics**: Two-ended insertion and deletion require symmetric handling of both ends.
- **Two-stack technique**: By transferring elements between stacks, two LIFOs can simulate FIFO queue behavior.
- **Local mins per stack**: Each element stores the minimum value present in its stack at insertion time, allowing O(1) minimum queries across both stacks.

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Dynamic range order-statistics in a mutable sequence is a practical problem appearing in text editors, collaborative applications, and database engines. It tests the ability to combine balanced binary search trees with order-statistics structures and manage update propagation carefully.

## Key Concepts
- Implicit data structures (position-based, not key-based)
- Range k-th statistics with duplicates
- Augmented BSTs (treap, red-black tree)
- Multiset or Fenwick tree per subtree node
- Coordinate compression for value domains

## Approach
An implicit treap stores the sequence by position, with each node augmented to contain a data structure representing all values in its subtree. When performing insertAt(i, v) or eraseAt(i), standard treap splits and merges propagate updates through O(log n) nodes, each updating its auxiliary structure in O(log n)—resulting in O(log² n) amortized time.

For rangeKth(l, r, k), split the treap into three segments, extract the middle [l, r] portion, and query the k-th smallest using the aggregated multisets or BIT at the root of that segment. After obtaining the answer, merge the three parts back together.

## Alternatives
A segment tree of multisets (or BITs over compressed values) provides similar complexity but with different trade-offs: more memory overhead for the explicit tree structure, but potentially simpler implementation and better cache locality.

## Complexity Summary
| Operation | Time | Space |
|-----------|------|-------|
| insertAt | O(log² n) | O(log n) per update |
| eraseAt | O(log² n) | O(log n) per update |
| rangeKth | O(log² n) | O(1) |

## Trade-offs
- **Implicit Treap**: Handles dynamic sequences naturally; splits/merges are built-in; slightly more complex augmentation logic
- **Segment Tree of BITs**: Better for static value domains; simpler overall structure; higher memory usage for dense trees

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question tests the ability to design a dynamic data structure supporting point queries on weighted interval sets. It assesses understanding of advanced tree structures, order statistics without enumeration, and handling of overlapping intervals and duplicates.

## Key Concepts
- **Segment tree over compressed coordinates**: Enables efficient range queries and updates
- **Per-node order-statistics structure**: Stores weights of all intervals fully covering the node's range
- **O(log N) node updates**: Each insertion, erasure, or weight update affects O(log N) segment tree nodes
- **Duplicate handling**: Intervals are distinguished by unique ids; weight updates and erasure operate on specific ids
- **Overlap handling**: Intervals partially covering a node are propagated to children; fully covered nodes store all overlapping intervals
- **K-th largest extraction**: Binary search on weight range combines counts from O(log N) nodes in O(log² N) without enumerating all intervals

## Why This Is Asked
This question evaluates a candidate's ability to design hybrid data structures that support dynamic 2D range queries with an additional color dimension, a common requirement in spatial analytics and geographic information systems.

## Key Concepts
- Dynamic 2D range structures (segment trees, range trees)
- Per-node multisets for color tracking and distinct counting
- Coordinate compression for memory efficiency
- Duplicate handling via color frequency counters
- Trade-offs between memory usage and query performance
- Lazy rebuilding strategies for coordinate space optimization

}
